At most four pure three-line triple points occur because each of six lines meets five other lines, two per pure triple (3t<=6floor(5/2)=12). Thus (0,7,4) needs at least three mixed triples but at most C(2,2)=1; (3,5,5) needs five pure triples but max four. For 2 cubics+3 lines with n2=0,n3=2,t5=8, the three lines must concur at one triple; the other triple comprises both cubics and a line, forcing cubic-cubic Bezout 9=1+3s, impossible mod3. Imported Talar free-degree-nine Tjurina and intersection formulas yield four potential types; independent integer enumeration reproduces candidates [(0,7,4),(3,5,5)] and [(0,2,8),(3,0,9)]. Consequence only the last remains necessary; no existence claimed.
